_comment: Declarative configuration for .cursor/hooks/guard_write_scope.py. Editing this file changes what the guard refuses. Keep it the single place where protected surfaces are named, so a boundary is never restated in prose in two places that can drift apart.
_comment_protected_path_globs: ADVISORY ONLY — NOT ENFORCED. No code reads this key: guard_write_scope.py inspects the command string and the branch, never the staged paths. It is retained because it records which surfaces a reviewer should look at, and it is labelled here because a key that looks like a boundary but refuses nothing is the same defect as a rule written in prose and enforced by nothing. Enforcing it was considered and rejected: the guard would have to refuse commits touching '.cursor/**' and 'state/**', which are the paths that configuration and control-plane lanes legitimately write, and an over-broad guard that blocks legitimate work is the first risk APPLY.md names. Do not read this list as protection.

refused_commands.reason: Pull-request writes are not a lane capability. In this estate a PR is a projection, never an acceptance, and lanes return branches rather than opening or moving pull requests.

This route's GitHub credential is read-only for everything except git contents. A write attempt here fails at GitHub anyway; refusing locally makes the boundary explicit instead of producing a confusing 403. Both -X and --method are matched, in either case, because a boundary that only catches one spelling is not a boundary.
Force push destroys the immutable-SHA custody the whole evidence ladder depends on. Use --force-with-lease only after an explicit instruction.
History rewriting breaks byte-for-byte read-back by immutable SHA, which is the property that makes produced evidence independently checkable.

_comment_detached_head: Refuse `git commit` while HEAD is detached. A commit on a detached HEAD advances no branch, which is how a lane's branch ref silently stays at the base while the lane believes it has committed.
_comment_stale_ref_push: Refuse `git push <branch>` when that branch sits on HEAD's own lineage and behind it. That is the exact signature of the silent no-op: git prints 'Everything up-to-date' and exits 0, so the exit code stops meaning the work was published. A divergent or unrelated branch is not refused, because pushing a different branch on purpose is legitimate.
